_comment: Source NAME -> Iron Codex article, for the interactive map (QUEUE 0v).
Hand-maintained. The map's build script resolves a polygon's NAME through this
table and NOWHERE else: there is no fuzzy matching, because a wrong link is
worse than a missing one (the rule tests/order-links.test.mjs already enforces
A name absent from this table still RENDERS on the map. It is drawn, named and
selectable, and its panel says no Codex article exists yet. Never drop a polygon
for lacking an article: blank ground would read as empty or unruled land, which
is the one thing the brief forbids.
'note' is shown in the polity panel. It exists for the cases where the polygon
and the article are not the same kind of thing - a dynasty rather than its realm,
an institution rather than its territory - because CLAUDE.md does not let a
people, a dynasty and a state be silently equated.
'dropFrom' removes a feature from named snapshot years only. It is for source
errors, and every entry has to say what the error is. Dropping is a last resort:
the ground then shows as unmapped, which is honest, where a stale label is not.

Emirate of Córdoba.note: The Codex has no article for the Emirate of Córdoba (756–929). This links to al-Andalus, the region. The Caliphate of Córdoba is a later state (929–1031) and is deliberately NOT linked here.

Papal States.note: The Papacy is an institution in the Codex, not a territory. The polygon is the temporal state it governed.

Eastern Roman Empire.note: The source's name for the state the Codex covers as the Byzantine Empire. Contemporaries called it Roman; 'Byzantine' is a later historians' label for the same polity.

Franks.note: The source labels this territory by the people. The link is to the kingdom, which is what a border on a map can actually show.

Ostrogoths.note: The source labels this territory by the people. The Ostrogoths are not the Ostrogothic Kingdom — the Codex keeps them apart — so the link is to the kingdom, whose borders these are.

Vandals.note: The source labels this territory by the people. The link is to the kingdom, not to the Vandals as a people.

Danube Bulgars.note: The state founded on the Danube in 681, which the Codex covers as the First Bulgarian Empire. The separate 'Bulgars' polygon at 600 is Old Great Bulgaria, a different polity, and is deliberately not linked here.

Seljuk Empire.note: The Codex article is the Great Seljuk Empire (1037–1194).

Almoravid dynasty.note: This is the dynasty, not the state it ruled. The Codex has no article for the Almoravid realm itself.

Teutonic Knights.note: The order's monastic state in Prussia. The Codex article is the order.

knownGaps.Fatimid Caliphate: No Codex article yet. In 1100 this is the largest unlinked territory on the map.
knownGaps.Granada: No article for the Emirate of Granada. The Codex's 'Granada' is the CITY, and linking a realm polygon to a city article would be wrong. The Nasrid dynasty has an article; the emirate does not.
knownGaps.Novgorod: No article for the Novgorod Republic. The Codex's 'Novgorod' is the CITY.
knownGaps.Mamluke Sultanate: No article. The Codex covers the preceding Ayyubid Sultanate only.
knownGaps.Venice: No article for the Republic of Venice.
knownGaps.Trebizond: No article for the Empire of Trebizond.
knownGaps.Poland-Lithuania: Deliberately unlinked. In 1400 this is the post-Krewo union; the Codex has separate Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania articles and picking one would misrepresent the other.
knownGaps.Bulgar Khanate: No article. The Codex's First Bulgarian Empire is a different, later state.
knownGaps.Western Roman Empire: No article for the Western Empire as a state. The Codex covers its end as an event, and the Romans as a people.
knownGaps.Visigoths: No article for the Visigothic Kingdom. The Codex has the Visigoths as a people, which is not the same thing and is not linked here.
knownGaps.Visigothic Kingdom: No article for the Visigothic Kingdom, only for the Visigoths as a people.
knownGaps.Bulgars: Old Great Bulgaria, which is not the First Bulgarian Empire the Codex covers. Deliberately unlinked.
knownGaps.Khazars: No article for the Khazar Khaganate.
knownGaps.Anglo-Saxons: A people, not a polity — and at this date not one state. The Codex covers the individual kingdoms.

Seljuk Caliphate.reason: Anachronism in the source. The Great Seljuk Empire ended in 1194 and the Sultanate of Rum in 1308; by 1400 this ground was Ottoman territory and the Anatolian beyliks. Publishing the label would put a state on the map 200 years after it fell.
